title: Clean Sheets and Checkpoints: Evidence Complexity for Certifying Sequential Agent Risk
abstract: arXiv:2610.39124v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Dangerous-capability evaluations often test an AI agent from prepared states at ordered milestones. A clean sheet records no successes. What it certifies about a campaign of $B$ attempts depends on what a failed attempt erases. We model the task as a chain of $k$ milestones divided into checkpoint segments and ask how many zero audit responses certify, at level $\alpha$, a completion probability of at most $\epsilon$. For segments chosen before the audit, counting possible completion windows gives a certificate for any specified budget. The bound also covers adaptive deployment processes that follow the chain's transitions, provided their success probabilities after every complete history are capped by the corresponding audit success probabilities. translated_title: 空白记录与检查点：认证序贯智能体风险的证据复杂度
translated_abstract: 危险能力评估通常从预先准备的状态出发，在有序的里程碑上对AI智能体进行测试。空白记录表示没有任何成功记录。它能为包含B次尝试的行动计划证明什么，取决于一次失败的尝试会抹去什么。我们将该任务建模为由k个里程碑组成的链并划分为检查点段，探究需要多少次零成功审计响应，才能在α显著性水平下证明完成概率至多为ε。对于在审计前选定的段，通过枚举可能的完成窗口，可为任意指定预算给出风险证书。该界限还可扩展至遵循链转移规则的自适应部署过程，前提是其每段完整历史之后的成功概率均被相应的审计成功概率所上界约束，而审计本身并不检验这一传输假设。在稀有风险阶段的内部，每个段要么在预算内极少被完成（活跃段），要么几乎总能被完成（空闲段）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于检查点段的审计框架，通过统计零成功审计响应的数量为序贯智能体的完成风险提供形式化统计证书，并刻画了稀有风险阶段中“活跃”与“空闲”段的结构特性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a checkpoint-based audit framework that certifies sequential agent completion risk by counting zero-success audit responses, characterizing the active/free segment structure in rare-risk regimes.
